encounters.cc: Scheduled psychiatric follow-up and preoperative consultation for elective inguinal hernia repair.

lines: Scheduled psychiatric follow-up and preoperative consultation for elective inguinal hernia repair.
He has been noncompliant with his antipsychotic medication for the past month.
His sister reports that he has been experiencing auditory hallucinations and believes that the television is sending him secret messages.
Today, he is scheduled to discuss elective hernia repair surgery due to a reducible inguinal hernia that causes discomfort during physical activity.
The patient has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension, which are well-controlled with metformin and lisinopril, respectively.
- Diphenhydramine 25 mg at bedtime as needed for sleep
- Calcium carbonate 500 mg as needed for dyspepsia
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 2 years ago, 10 pack-year history.
The patient appears disheveled, with poor eye contact and intermittent mumbling to himself.
On examination, the patient is alert but appears to be responding to internal stimuli.
Physical examination is unremarkable except for the known inguinal hernia.

encounters.cc: Progressive fatigue and exertional dyspnea over the past 3 months.

lines: Progressive fatigue and exertional dyspnea over the past 3 months.
The patient, evaluated six months ago for psychiatric preoperative hernia consultation, presents to the clinic with a 3-month history of progressive fatigue and exertional dyspnea.
He denies any chest pain, palpitations, or syncope.
He has a past medical history of hypertension and peptic ulcer disease.
His medications include lisinopril and occasional over-the-counter antacids.
- Diphenhydramine 25 mg at bedtime as needed for sleep
- Calcium carbonate 500 mg as needed for dyspepsia
He has a 10-year history of smoking one pack of cigarettes per day but quit 2 years ago.
On physical examination, his skin and conjunctivae are pale.

encounters.cc: Excessive daytime sleepiness, near-miss motor vehicle collision, and witnessed apneic episodes during sleep.

lines: Excessive daytime sleepiness, near-miss motor vehicle collision, and witnessed apneic episodes during sleep.
The patient with schizophrenia and iron deficiency anemia evaluated in July 2020 presents with excessive daytime sleepiness.
He reports that he has nearly fallen asleep at the wheel on multiple occasions, including a recent minor motor vehicle collision.
His wife reports loud snoring and has witnessed him stop breathing at night.
He admits to occasionally taking diphenhydramine to help with sleep.
- Calcium carbonate 500 mg as needed for dyspepsia
His BMI is 32 kg/m^2. His blood pressure is 145/90 mmHg.
His neck circumference is 17 inches. Physical examination reveals crowded oropharynx.
The patient's Epworth Sleepiness Scale score is 16 (out of 24), indicating severe daytime sleepiness.

encounters.cc: Progressive weight gain, worsening hypertension, proximal muscle weakness, and facial plethora developing over 4 months.

lines: Progressive weight gain, worsening hypertension, proximal muscle weakness, and facial plethora developing over 4 months.
The patient with hypertension, schizophrenia, and diabetes, previously evaluated for sleep apnea and anemia, presents with symptoms progressing over the past 4 months.
He notes increased fat around his face and neck, easy bruising, poor wound healing, intermittent diplopia, and difficulty rising from chairs.
- Diphenhydramine 25 mg at bedtime as needed for sleep
- Calcium carbonate 500 mg as needed for dyspepsia
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 2 years ago, 10 pack-year history.
On neurologic exam, his deep tendon reflexes are slightly diminished but improve after brief exercise.
He is able to maintain upward gaze for 60 seconds without ptosis.
Labs show elevated serum cortisol and elevated ACTH levels.
A low-dose dexamethasone test fails to suppress cortisol.

encounters.cc: Six-week history of neck pain with intermittent tingling in the left arm exacerbated by movement.

lines: Six-week history of neck pain with intermittent tingling in the left arm exacerbated by movement.
The patient with schizophrenia and hernia history presents with neck pain.
He reports the pain is exacerbated by turning his head to the left and by lifting heavy objects at work.
His medical history is significant for hypertension, controlled with lisinopril.
- Diphenhydramine 25 mg at bedtime as needed for sleep
- Calcium carbonate 500 mg as needed for dyspepsia
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 2 years ago, 10 pack-year history.
On physical examination, there is tenderness to palpation over the left paracervical musculature.
The patient exhibits weakness during left arm biceps and wrist extensor strength testing.
The biceps reflex is diminished on the left side.
Sensation is decreased over the left thumb and index finger.
- Complete blood count: within normal limits
- Erythrocyte sedimentation rate: within normal limits
An MRI of the cervical spine reveals a herniated disc at the C6-C7 level with nerve root impingement.

encounters.cc: Worsening fatigue, headaches, dizziness, and compulsive water consumption resulting in polydipsia.

lines: Worsening fatigue, headaches, dizziness, and compulsive water consumption resulting in polydipsia.
This 50-year-old male with schizophrenia and ectopic ACTH production presents with increased water intake.
She notes that he has been more withdrawn recently, spending most of his time at home, and has been drinking large amounts of water throughout the day.
He carries a water bottle with him everywhere and wakes up multiple times at night to drink.
He has not seen his psychiatrist in several months, as he discontinued follow-up stating he felt “controlled by the government.”
- Cervical radiculopathy due to C6-C7 disc herniation (diagnosed 2023-01-15)
- Diphenhydramine 25 mg at bedtime as needed for sleep
- Calcium carbonate 500 mg as needed for dyspepsia
He lives alone after retiring early.
He denies nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, recent illness, or changes in appetite.
Temperature is normal, blood pressure is 122/78 mmHg, and pulse is 80/min.
On examination, he appears thin, with dry skin and flat affect.

encounters.cc: Sudden onset of severe periumbilical abdominal pain with associated low-grade fever and recent unintentional weight loss.

lines: Sudden onset of severe periumbilical abdominal pain with associated low-grade fever and recent unintentional weight loss.
The patient is a 51-year-old male with chronic hepatitis B, schizophrenia, type 2 diabetes, and reducible inguinal hernia who presents with severe abdominal pain that began suddenly 6 hours ago.
The pain is localized to the periumbilical region and is described as sharp and constant.
He also reports a low-grade fever and a recent unintentional weight loss of 10 pounds over the past month.
- Cervical radiculopathy due to C6-C7 disc herniation (diagnosed 2023-01-15)
His past medical history is significant for hypertension.
- Diphenhydramine 25 mg at bedtime as needed for sleep
- Calcium carbonate 500 mg as needed for dyspepsia
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 2 years ago, 10 pack-year history.
Blood pressure is 145/90 mmHg, heart rate is 98 beats per minute, and temperature is 38.1°C (100.6°F)
Abdominal examination reveals tenderness to palpation in the periumbilical area with no rebound or guarding.
There is no jaundice or rash.
An abdominal CT scan with contrast shows no evidence of appendicitis, cholecystitis, or pancreatitis but reveals multiple small aneurysms and irregular narrowing of the mesenteric arteries.

encounters.cc: Severe pain, discoloration, and tissue necrosis of fingers after prolonged cold exposure during snowstorm.

lines: Severe pain, discoloration, and tissue necrosis of fingers after prolonged cold exposure during snowstorm.
The 52-year-old male with schizophrenia, diabetes, and prior polyarteritis nodosa presents after he was stranded overnight in his car during a snowstorm.
He reports that he was unable to keep the car heater running and did not have gloves.
- Cervical radiculopathy due to C6-C7 disc herniation (diagnosed 2023-01-15)
His past medical history is significant for hypertension, controlled with lisinopril.
- Diphenhydramine 25 mg at bedtime as needed for sleep
- Calcium carbonate 500 mg as needed for dyspepsia
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 2 years ago, 10 pack-year history.
His temperature is 35.6°C (96.1°F), blood pressure is 135/85 mmHg, pulse is 88 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 16 beats per minute.
On examination, his fingers are cold, mottled, and have a waxy appearance.
There is no active bleeding or blister formation.
Sensation is decreased, and capillary refill is absent in the affected fingers.
The rest of the physical examination is unremarkable.
Initial management includes rapid rewarming of his fingers in a warm water bath at 40°C (104°F) for 30 minutes.
Despite rewarming, the patient's fingers remain discolored with persistent sensory loss and absent capillary refill.
